lines.text: Paul says Christ set us free for freedom, so stand firm and don't be weighed down again by a yoke of slavery, because if they let themselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to them at all (Galatians 5:1-2).

Paul testifies that a man who gets himself circumcised is obligated to obey the whole law, and that anyone trying to be justified by the law has been severed from Christ and has fallen away from grace (Galatians 5:3-4).
Paul says that by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of glory, and that in Christ Jesus what matters is faith expressing itself through love (Galatians 5:5-6).

Paul tells them they were running so well, asks who obstructed them, and warns that a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough, while the one troubling them will bear the judgment (Galatians 5:7-10).

Paul says they were called to freedom, so serve one another in love, because the entire law is fulfilled in a single decree, which is to remember the Sabbath day, and he warns them to watch out, or they will be consumed by one another if they keep on biting and devouring one another (Galatians 5:13-15).
